comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PHASE 1 ROOT CAUSE — CONFIRMED BY RUNTIME OBSERVATION (rebar-debug). No live Jira was touched.

## Mechanism (confirmed)

`pytest-xdist` reads the `xdist_group` mark in exactly ONE scheduler. Installed xdist 3.8.0:
`xdist/scheduler/loadgroup.py:11-47` is the only scheduler that computes a group scope;
`scheduler/load.py` and `scheduler/worksteal.py` contain **zero** occurrences of `group`
(`grep -c group` returns 0 for both). Under any other `--dist` mode the mark is parsed
(`xdist/remote.py:245`) and then discarded — no error, no warning. Silently inert.

## Discriminating experiment (RUNTIME, not source-reading)

8 tests marked `xdist_group("live_reconcile_e2e")` + 8 unmarked tests, `-n 4`, each test
recording `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` to a file. Same tests, three dist modes, this worktree's venv
(xdist 3.8.0). Observed worker placement of the 8 GROUPED tests:

    --dist load        -> gw0 gw0 gw1 gw1 gw2 gw2 gw3 gw3   (scattered over 4 workers)
    --dist worksteal   -> gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0 gw1 gw1 gw1 gw1   (scattered over 2 workers)
    --dist loadgroup   -> gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0 gw0   (confined to 1 worker)

The `loadgroup` arm is the negative control: it proves xdist, the mark, and the harness are all
working, so the scattering under `load`/`worksteal` is the scheduler ignoring the group and not a
broken probe. This discriminates "the mark is inert outside loadgroup" from "the mark never
works" and from "xdist is misconfigured here".

The same run also proves the (b) half: under `--dist loadgroup`, the UNGROUPED tests landed on
gw1/gw2/gw3 **while** the grouped set occupied gw0 — i.e. an ungrouped live-Jira test runs
CONCURRENTLY with the confined group even in the CI lane that does pass `--dist loadgroup`.

## Where the invariant actually breaks

Two independent breaks, one shared cause:

(a) NO configured local invocation honours the group. `pyproject.toml:599` sets only
    `addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config"` — no `-n`, no `--dist`; there is no
    `pytest.ini`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini`. So an ad-hoc `pytest -n auto` gets xdist's default
    `--dist load`, and the documented local command (`docs/coverage.md:47`) is
    `--dist worksteal`. Both ignore the group. Note this is BROADER than the ticket's framing:
    worksteal, not just load, drops it — and worksteal is what the project documents.

(b) A live-Jira test carries no group at all.
    `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py:155` `test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira` is
    `@pytest.mark.integration` and issues a real project-wide inbound JQL fetch whenever `acli`
    is on PATH and `JIRA_PROJECT` is set. It has no `xdist_group`. Because it IS in the
    integration tier, it runs in CI's `--dist loadgroup` lane — and, per the experiment above,
    lands on a different worker from the E2E group. So this break is live in CI's own lane, not
    only locally.

Corroborating the ticket's note: `test_delete_permission_probe`
(`tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py:334`) is the ONLY `@_requires_live` test in its
module — every other test there is offline/deterministic. So the intra-module group buys nothing
by itself; the counterparty it needs to be serialised against is precisely the ungrouped test in
(b).

## Legitimacy: `defect` (not intended behaviour, not a feature request)

Cited authority — story 8d36 `curricular-brickred-ratfish` (8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd, CLOSED), which
introduced xdist parallelism, states the invariant in its own description:

  "Integration tier: parallelize only NON-live tests. ... Live tests ([integration, live], e.g.
   test_reconcile_live_e2e.py) share one live Jira project and flake under parallel load
   (eventual-consistency); keep them serial or confine to one worker via
   @pytest.mark.xdist_group + --dist loadgroup. In CI's integration job they self-skip without
   Jira creds, BUT THE COMMAND MUST NOT ASSUME THAT."

and its commit body (f943c7ef58): "test_reconcile_live_e2e.py: xdist_group so the live-Jira
reconciler E2E stays serial". The shipped code takes the confinement arm, so the invariant it
must hold is "every live-Jira-touching test is group-confined, wherever it can run". Both (a) and
(b) violate it. The final clause of 8d36 forecloses the obvious defence ("they skip in CI").

I checked the not-a-bug case before concluding. The strongest one available is that the E2E
module docstring (lines 59-63) DOES name loadgroup — "even when the integration tier is
parallelized with `-n>0 --dist loadgroup`" — so it is not simply lying, which is a real point
against AC1's "correct the docstring" arm as stated. But the same comment then closes with "so
this only matters on a local live run", and a local live run is exactly the context where no
loadgroup is configured. The comment promises the protection precisely where it is absent. That
is a defect against 8d36's invariant, not a doc nit.

## Harm today: LATENT, not active — and that shapes the fix

Being straight about this, because it drives urgency:
- In CI, both live tests self-skip (no `acli`, no creds). No traffic, so no collision today.
- `make test` is `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q` — serial, and it deselects
  the live tests anyway. The documented local coverage command deselects them too.
- So no CURRENTLY-CONFIGURED invocation actually runs two live-Jira tests concurrently.
- But the exposure is real and this project has stood in it: d30c's regression comment records a
  "complete local xdist inventory with live Jira credentials present" on 2026-08-18 — an ad-hoc
  full-suite xdist run with creds is a thing that happens here. In that run the two live tests
  share one Jira Cloud account's rate budget and one project's search index, and the E2E probe's
  whole assertion is about index convergence timing.

I did NOT attempt a live-Jira reproduction: the bridge is paused for a duplicate-comment cleanup
and any write would interfere. The harm claim is therefore reasoned exposure, not an observed
collision, and I am labelling it as such rather than overstating it.

Consequence for the fix: the right move is to restore the invariant cheaply and make its absence
LOUD — not to re-architect scheduling. Specifically, I am NOT putting `--dist loadgroup` into
`pyproject.toml` addopts, as AC1 suggests as one option. Three reasons: (1) it re-schedules all
~14k tests in every local `-n` run, discarding worksteal's dynamic rebalancing that 8d36 chose
deliberately and docs/coverage.md documents; (2) addopts are PREPENDED, so CI's explicit
`--dist worksteal` still wins — the setting would look like protection while doing nothing in the
lane it appears to cover; (3) it does not fix (b) at all.

## Defect origin (caused_by)

**8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd** (`curricular-brickred-ratfish`), commit **f943c7ef58** (2026-07-13),
trailer `rebar-ticket: 8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd`. That commit introduced `-n` + `--dist` and added the
`xdist_group` mark — i.e. it CREATED the obligation and shipped without meeting it for the second
live-Jira test. Before it, nothing ran in parallel, so live-Jira traffic was serialised by
construction; after it, it is not. Classified `regression` on that basis.

Divergence from what a mechanical blame would say, recorded per protocol: this is an UNMET
OBLIGATION, so the fix site is not the cause site. `git blame` on
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` names 7a7a439309 (2026-06-15, "split tests/interfaces into
seam subdirectories") — a file-move carrier, and one that PREDATES the transition, which is the
date test failing. That test's lines were correct when written; they became wrong when 8d36 added
parallelism around them. Attributing to the consumer's old commit would charge the defect to the
wrong work item. `88cc31390c` (2b60) is likewise a carrier — it only relocated the `--dist
loadgroup` line into a reusable workflow. Searches run: `git log -S'--dist loadgroup'`,
`git log -S'xdist_group("live_reconcile_e2e")'`, `git log -S'test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira'`.

comments.body:
PHASE 2 COMPLETE — rebar-debug final report. Gerrit change 1963 (commit a13190d82c) is up for
review. No live Jira was touched at any point: every probe used `--collect-only`, so no test
body ran and no Jira request was issued.

## Test (RED -> GREEN, held out from the fixer)

`tests/unit/test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py` — five tests, written and seen RED BEFORE any
fix existed, then physically moved out of the tree so the implementing subagent could not read
or edit it. It was handed only the proven mechanism and a contract card.

Legitimately RED first, for the right reason in both cases:
- the AST policy scan failed naming exactly one offender,
  `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py::test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira`, no false
  positives;
- the behavioural subprocess test failed with the unsafe configuration SILENTLY ACCEPTED —
  exit 0, "16 tests collected" — which is the defect itself, not an import or fixture error.
Three negative controls (loadgroup accepted, serial accepted, no-credentials silent) passed
before the fix and still pass after, so the guard's no-op cases are pinned too.

Teeth confirmed by three defect-seeded mutations, each re-introducing a confirmed cause and
each returning a DIFFERENT test to RED:
- re-remove the `xdist_group` decorator -> the policy scan goes RED;
- neuter the loadgroup check (`if dist == "loadgroup"` -> always-safe) -> the behavioural test
  goes RED;
- neuter the credentials check -> `test_guard_stays_silent_without_live_jira_credentials` goes
  RED, proving the CI-safety no-op is genuinely asserted and not incidental.

Refactoring litmus: the subprocess tests assert observable output (exit code + message text),
not internals — renaming `unconfined_live_jira_reason` does not break them.

## Fix

- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` — `@pytest.mark.xdist_group("live_reconcile_e2e")` on
  `test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira` (function decorator; module-scope `pytestmark`
  would be wrong, the file is overwhelmingly non-live).
- `tests/_live_jira_confinement.py` (new) — a PURE predicate
  `unconfined_live_jira_reason(config, items) -> str | None`. Returns a message only when the
  run is parallel AND the scheduler is not `loadgroup` AND live credentials plus `acli` are
  ACTUALLY present AND at least one collected item carries the group. Every other combination
  is a silent no-op. Kept out of conftest so it is callable without spawning pytest (and
  conftest is near this project's 800-line cap).
- `tests/conftest.py` — arm (c) on the existing `pytest_collection_modifyitems`, beside the
  bug-4a48 external-confinement guard it is modelled on. It raises `pytest.UsageError` rather
  than `pytest.fail`: this arm can only fire under `-n>0`, and from the xdist controller a
  `pytest.fail` escapes as a 20-line `INTERNALERROR>` traceback that buries the remedy under a
  stack the reader did not cause. I checked this empirically before changing it. The condition
  IS a usage error, so `UsageError` gives a clean `ERROR: …` banner at exit 4. A guard whose
  entire value is a legible message must not look like a crash.
- `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` — comment-only. The old text closed "they also
  self-skip without live creds, so this only matters on a local live run", which promised
  protection exactly where it is absent. It now states the mark is honoured ONLY under
  `--dist loadgroup`, that other schedulers discard it silently, and that the guard covers the
  rest.

Explicitly NOT done: pinning `--dist loadgroup` in `pyproject.toml` addopts (AC1's suggested
option). Reasons in the RCA comment — addopts are prepended so CI's explicit `--dist worksteal`
still wins (fake protection in the very lane it appears to cover), it reschedules ~15k tests in
every local `-n` run, and it fixes neither gap.

## Replication of the original report

Run on THIS machine, which turns out to have live Jira credentials AND `acli` on PATH — i.e.
it is itself an instance of the exposed configuration, which is corroborating evidence for the
harm premise rather than a hypothetical.

- `pytest --collect-only -n auto` (the reporter's "complete local xdist inventory"; `auto`
  resolved to `-n 18` here, incidentally confirming docs/coverage.md's over-subscription
  warning) -> BEFORE: silently accepted. AFTER: exit 4 with the violation and the remedy.
- `pytest --collect-only -n 4` (bare, so xdist's default `--dist load`) -> exit 4.
- `pytest --collect-only -n 4 --dist loadgroup` -> exit 0, 15168 tests collected; the safe path
  is unobstructed.
- The group now holds **17** items where it held 16, which is the direct end-to-end proof that
  the previously-ungrouped live test joined it.

The original report no longer reproduces: the silent inertness is gone in every mode.

## Scope & safety

- Caller-dependency sweep: clear. Nothing references
  `test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira` outside its own definition. The one caller that
  invokes a `pytest_collection_modifyitems` with `config=None`
  (`tests/unit/test_external_canary.py:92,100`) loads `tests/external/conftest.py`, NOT the root
  conftest, so it is untouched — I verified the import target rather than assuming from the
  symbol name.
- Restoration, not creation: no new entry point, user-visible artifact, or mutating external
  call. The guard is test infrastructure, and AC3 of this ticket is its design authority.
- No new dependency. No test weakened — the two edits to existing test files are one decorator
  plus comments; no assertion removed, none loosened, no skip/xfail added.

## Step 7 sweep

Axis 1 (construct). The new AST scan IS the repo-wide sweep for "a live-Jira-reaching test
without the group mark": it walks all of `tests/` except `tests/external/` and found exactly one
live instance, now fixed. One related-but-distinct construct found:
`xdist_group("large_ticket_server")` on two tests in
`tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py:334,348` is inert under the same conditions.
Disposition: ACCEPTED, not fixed. It confines a LOCAL git-server fixture, so scattering costs
duplicate fixture setup, not correctness — a different severity class from racing a shared
external system.

Axis 2 (parity). Rule, stated without reference to the fixed site: "a test that can reach the
shared live Jira must be serialised against every other such test." Census over the surfaces
this rule can have — the test lanes, since this is a test-infra rule with no CLI/MCP/library
surface:
- default tier — `--dist worksteal`, but deselects `integration`, so no group item is ever
  collected. N/A.
- integration tier — `--dist loadgroup`. Covered by the added mark.
- external tier (`tests/external/`) — its own credential-scoped workflow job;
  `external-integration.yml` passes NO `-n` and NO `--dist`, so it is serial by construction.
  Verified, not assumed. N/A.
- e2e tier — no live Jira. N/A.
- dual-direction (a live-Jira test reaching Jira by some path other than `acli`) — probed every
  non-external test referencing `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN`; all are hermetic/mocked, and
  `tests/unit` + `tests/scripts` are socket-guarded by conftest's network guard. `acli` is the
  reconciler's only Jira transport. No MISSING slot.

## Residual risk

1. The detector keys on `which("acli")`. A future live-Jira test reaching Jira over direct HTTP
   would evade it. ACCEPTED: no such transport exists — `acli` is the reconciler's only Jira
   path, so adding one would be a deliberate architectural change that should carry its own
   confinement review.
2. `large_ticket_server`'s inert group, above. ACCEPTED, cost not correctness.
3. The guard cannot protect a machine with credentials that runs the live tests SERIALLY against
   a Jira project someone else is concurrently using. Out of scope: that is cross-process, not
   cross-worker.

## Gates

`make lint` PASS; `make typecheck` PASS (598 files); `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` ->
`active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`. Pre-commit hook (lint + typecheck + 50/72 message wrap)
passed on commit. CI workflows untouched — the `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` hang
guards and every existing `-n`/`--dist` argument are unchanged.

Local full default-suite run: started, and being left to run as corroboration, but it is slow on
this host (~15k tests) and CI's four-cell matrix is the authoritative broad regression oracle.
The ticket will NOT be closed before `Verified +1`.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FULL-SUITE RESULT + a real defect the suite caught in my own test (patchset 2 of Gerrit 1963).

Ran the complete default tier locally: `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4
--dist worksteal` -> **14821 passed, 55 skipped, 1 xfailed, 1 failed, 4 errors** in 18m24s.
Reporting the non-green results rather than rounding them off, because one of them was mine.

## The 1 failure was REAL and it was my new test's fault

`tests/unit/test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py::test_all_non_fixture_subprocess_environments_use_the_safe_boundary`
failed, naming `tests/unit/test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py:143` — the held-out test I wrote.
Its subprocess helper built the child environment as a plain `dict(os.environ)`. This repo
forbids that: pytest prints call arguments in its default long traceback, so a plain dict dumps
every inherited environment value if subprocess startup ever fails. The boundary is
`tests/_subprocess_env.py`'s `subprocess_env()`, whose `SubprocessEnv.__repr__` redacts.

That policy is pointed squarely at this test. It injects fake `JIRA_*` values, and it runs on
hosts that carry REAL Jira credentials — this one does. A startup failure would have printed
them. Fixed in patchset 2: `env = subprocess_env()`, with a comment recording why.

Worth stating plainly: `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the complexity ratchet were all green
across this the whole time. Only the broader suite caught it. This is exactly the case for not
treating the fast gates as sufficient — and I would have shipped it had I stopped at them.

## The 4 errors were self-inflicted, not regressions

All four were `Failed: Test moved the repo HEAD (987caf8c73 -> a13190d82c)`. I committed the fix
WHILE the suite was running, so tests that assert the repo HEAD is stable saw it move underneath
them. My own process artifact, not a defect in the change. Confirmed by re-running all four with
HEAD stable: **4 passed**. The lesson is procedural (don't commit mid-suite), and I am recording
it rather than quietly re-running until green — per this project's rule that a retry is not a
diagnosis.

## Re-verification after the patchset-2 edit

Because I touched the held-out test, I re-ran its teeth rather than assuming they survived. All
three defect-seeded mutations still return it to RED, each on a different assertion:
- re-remove the `xdist_group` decorator -> the AST policy scan goes RED;
- neuter the loadgroup check -> the behavioural test goes RED;
- neuter the credentials check -> the CI-safety no-op test goes RED.
The oracle itself: 5 passed. `test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py`: 20 passed. Gates re-run
green (`lint`, `typecheck`, `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`).

Patchset 2 carries the same Change-Id (I2658b614...), so it is a new patchset on 1963, not a
duplicate change. `LLM-Review +1` was cast on patchset 1; both votes will re-run against
patchset 2, and the ticket stays in_progress until `Verified +1`.

comments.body:
CLOSED — merged and verified. Gerrit 1963 landed on `origin/main` as 897ae2e1c4 (rebased sha;
authored locally as a13190d82c under Rebase-If-Necessary). Both gates confirmed by direct REST
query rather than taken on report: `LLM-Review +1` (rebar review bot), `Verified +1` (rebar CI
bot), change status MERGED, and the commit is reachable from a worktree fast-forwarded to
origin/main. Closed `--class=regression --caused-by=8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd`.

## Acceptance criteria — all three met by landed code

- AC1 (pin the mode OR correct the docstring): took the docstring arm and went further. The
  comment now states the mark is honoured ONLY under `--dist loadgroup`. The addopts arm was
  deliberately NOT taken: addopts are prepended, so CI's explicit `--dist worksteal` would
  still win — it would have been protection in appearance only.
- AC2 (group the second live test): done; end-to-end proof is the group going 16 -> 17 members.
- AC3 (a guard for future live tests): `test_every_live_jira_test_is_xdist_group_confined`,
  mutation-verified.

Ticking the boxes changed ONLY checkbox characters — verified by diffing the before/after
descriptions with both box states normalised to the same token, which came back identical. This
ticket carried no plan-review attestation (`signature: null`) in any case.

## Reproduced bug 10d0-c26c-bdbb-4b1f (ruling-magnific-bats) on this close

Passing `--caused-by` when an identical `caused_by` edge already existed created a SECOND
duplicate edge to the same target — link_uuids 8b828d0a (from the earlier `rebar link`) and
93b33884 (from the close). This is a third confirmed occurrence of that defect. Removed the
duplicate with `rebar unlink … caused_by`, which removed exactly one edge as documented; **one
`caused_by` edge to 8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd now remains**, verified after the fact.

Worth noting for that bug's own RCA: passing the flag is still right despite the duplicate. An
empty `--caused-by` re-runs blame auto-derivation unconditionally, and here blame would have
named a June file-move carrier in `test_cli.py` — a wrong edge, which is a worse input to the
escape-rate metric than a duplicate correct one.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

Two independent gaps make the live-Jira E2E tests' isolation story weaker than the code claims.

### (a) `xdist_group` is inert under the distribution mode a local full-suite run actually uses

`tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py:62-66` carries
`pytest.mark.xdist_group("live_reconcile_e2e")`, and the module docstring (lines ~57-61) states this
"pins every test in this module to a SINGLE pytest-xdist worker".

That is true **only under `--dist loadgroup`**. Verified against the installed xdist 3.8.0:
`xdist/scheduler/loadgroup.py:11-13` is the only scheduler that reads groups; `scheduler/load.py`
and `scheduler/worksteal.py` contain zero occurrences of `group`/`xdist_group`, and
`xdist/plugin.py:124` documents the mark as loadgroup-only.

CI passes `--dist loadgroup` for the integration tier (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:663`),
so CI is fine. But `pyproject.toml:599` sets only `addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config"` —
no `-n`, no `--dist` — so a local `pytest -n auto` (exactly the "full local xdist inventory" that
produced the d30c regression report) gets xdist's **default `--dist load`, where the group mark is
silently ignored**. The protection the docstring promises does not exist locally.

### (b) A second live-Jira test carries no group mark at all

`tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py:155-172` — `test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira` — runs a
real `rebar reconcile` dry-run against live Jira whenever `acli` is on PATH and `JIRA_PROJECT` is
set. It has no `xdist_group` and no `pytestmark` (a repo-wide `xdist_group` grep returns only
`test_reconcile_live_e2e.py:65` and `test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py:334,348`). It can therefore
land on a different worker and issue a project-wide inbound JQL fetch concurrently with the
delete-permission probe's create+poll — under `loadgroup` **and** under `load`.

Note also that `test_delete_permission_probe` is the only `@_requires_live` test inside its own
module, so the intra-module grouping buys nothing on its own; the counterparty it needs to be
serialised against lives in a different file.

## Not the d30c root cause

d30c's failure was fully explained and fixed without any load term (the poll's per-JQL memo made it
a single-shot check). This ticket is the separately-observed isolation gap, filed so it is not lost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Either pin the distribution mode so `xdist_group` is honoured wherever the live tests can run
  (e.g. set `--dist loadgroup` in `pyproject.toml` addopts), or correct the module docstring so it
  no longer claims protection that only holds in CI.
- [x] Put `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py::test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira` in the
  same xdist group as the live reconciler E2E module, so all live-Jira traffic serialises.
- [x] A test or guard that fails if a new live-Jira-touching test is added without the group mark.
compiled_state.title: Live-Jira test isolation: xdist_group is ignored under the default --dist load, and a second live test is ungrouped
